requirements.label: Historically limited to ages 17 to 29
requirements.source_quote: Applicants must be proficient in basic math and reading skills, have a high school diploma or GED, and be between the ages of 17-29.

data_quality_flags.note: This program is listed here specifically because a directory would list it and a person would waste a week on it. Three signals conflict. Secondary sources report the program stopped offering courses in 2023. The live site carries a 2026 copyright and Get Started and Join Now calls to action, implying it is active. But the site's own published contact details are unfilled template placeholders, which is not what an actively recruiting program looks like. This registry does not resolve the conflict. It surfaces it, and routes the person to a program they can actually start.

The age range comes from a third-party bootcamp review site, not from the program itself. It is recorded as unverified. If accurate, it would exclude many career changers, which is a material eligibility question and not a detail to discover after applying.

funding_paths.name: WIOA training scholarship
funding_paths.full_name: Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act training scholarship
funding_paths.covers: Some workforce training program costs, for people who qualify
funding_paths.determined_by: Local Alabama Career Centers, not the training provider
funding_paths.determined_by_source_quote: Local Alabama Career Centers provide WIOA (Workforce Investment Opportunity Act) scholarship opportunities to qualifying students for some workforce training programs. Eligibility is based on various factors, including income.

ordering_constraint.why: Jefferson State requires payment online at the time of enrollment, and WIOA eligibility is determined by the Career Center rather than by the college. A person who enrolls first has already paid, and a person who waits to ask about funding until the cohort opens has run out of time. The eligibility conversation has to start first.
